title: H-1B Workers Taking Microsoft Buyout Face 60-Day Deadline to Stay
excerpt: Microsoft has not said whether H-1B holders are eligible for its voluntary exit offer to 60,000 employees. For visa workers who do accept and leave on December 31, USCIS rules give up to 60 days to find a new sponsor, change status, or depart.
body:
• Microsoft announced a Voluntary Exit Offer on October 26, 2026, open to about 60,000 employees at level 70 and below in participating organizations in the United States, Canada, India and the United Kingdom.
  • The company has not said whether workers holding an H-1B visa qualify, how many visa holders are eligible, or whether it will offer immigration-related assistance.
  • Eligible employees have until the first week of December to decide, and workers who accept are expected to leave by year-end, on December 31.
  • Reader utility: if an H-1B worker leaves on December 31, USCIS allows up to 60 consecutive days after employment ends, or until the I-94 expires, whichever is shorter, to be the beneficiary of a new employer petition, file a change of status, file for adjustment of status, or apply for a compelling circumstances work permit.

Microsoft's voluntary buyout, covered by The Videshi in Microsoft Offers Voluntary Buyouts to 60,000 Employees Across Four Countries, raises a separate question for employees whose right to live in the United States depends on the job itself. Accepting the exit package ends the employment that supports H-1B status. That consequence, not the severance terms, is the decision H-1B workers have to weigh before the early December deadline.

Chief People Officer Amy Coleman announced the program in a staff memo. VisaVerge reported that the offer covers eligible workers in participating organizations, including AI experiences, Copilot, Windows + Devices, Xbox, finance and human resources, while marketing, commercial business, sales and some engineering groups are not participating.

"This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs."

— Amy Coleman, Chief People Officer, Microsoft

What Microsoft Has Not Said on Visas

Visa-specific terms remain unresolved. According to VisaVerge, Microsoft has not said how many visa holders may be eligible or whether it will offer immigration-related assistance. TechResearchOnline put the point plainly for Indian employees in the United States: workers on H-1B visas who accept must find another company to sponsor their stay or change their immigration status to remain in the country.

The package itself, as reported by both outlets, includes base pay tied to tenure and level, continued stock vesting, limited healthcare coverage and career-transition services. Those benefits do not extend immigration status.

The 60-Day Rule After Employment Ends

Under the rules summarized by USCIS in its FAQs for individuals in H-1B status, when employment is terminated, either voluntarily or involuntarily, a worker typically may take one of several actions to remain in a period of authorized stay in the United States. USCIS lists filing an application for a change of nonimmigrant status, filing an application for adjustment of status, filing an application for a compelling circumstances Employment Authorization Document, or being the beneficiary of a nonfrivolous petition to change employer.

If one of those actions occurs within the up-to-60-day grace period, USCIS says the period of authorized stay can exceed 60 days, even if the worker loses the previous status. If no action is taken, the worker and any dependents may need to depart within 60 days, or when the authorized validity period ends, whichever is shorter. VisaVerge gave the same boundary: up to 60 days after paid employment ends, or until the I-94 expires, whichever comes first, and the period may be shortened by USCIS and used only once per H-1B validity period.

The clock matters for the December 31 exit date. The period runs after employment ends, not from the October announcement or the December decision deadline, which is why H-1B employees cannot assess the offer on severance alone without also lining up a sponsor, a change-of-status filing, or a departure plan.

A Complicated Backdrop on Sponsorship

The buyout also lands after a separate federal action. VisaVerge reported that on October 8, the Labor Department suspended Microsoft, Adobe and six IT outsourcers from the PERM program, which employers use to sponsor foreign workers for green cards. That action did not cancel existing H-1B status, and no connection between the suspension and the exit offer has been reported.

What to Watch Next

The immediate test is clarification. If Microsoft confirms whether H-1B holders are eligible and whether any immigration support accompanies the package, affected workers will have firmer ground for the December decision. Until then, the sources agree on the core fact: the company has offered an exit to a large pool of employees, and it has not publicly answered the visa question. Workers considering the offer can review the options listed by VisaVerge in its coverage of the offer and by USCIS, and should take individual advice before accepting, because eligibility, I-94 dates and pending filings differ by case.

steps.step: Be the beneficiary of a new employer petition
steps.detail: A new employer timely files a nonfrivolous petition to change employer within the up to 60-day grace period, according to USCIS.

steps.step: File an application for a change of nonimmigrant status
steps.detail: USCIS lists this as an action that, if taken within the grace period, can extend authorized stay beyond 60 days.

steps.step: File an application for adjustment of status
steps.detail: Available if eligible, according to USCIS.

steps.step: File for a compelling circumstances Employment Authorization Document
steps.detail: USCIS lists this as a further option for eligible workers.
